ui_rules: Preserve the approved DocForge workbench layout and light-theme visual language.
Replace thesis-specific project identity, labels, filenames, file filters, diagnostics, and help text with DocForge and document terminology.
Do not add a theme switcher, locale switcher, new screen, or redesigned layout.
Cover the existing desktop and mobile workbench in sensory verification after terminology changes.
architecture_modules: Generic project manifest and path model for docforge.yaml and docforge.project.v1.
ForgeDocument core aggregate and generic metadata with an optional typed academic profile.
Parser, validator, template resolver, compiler, RenderPlan, bibliography, DOCX renderer, Review, and BuildReport pipeline.
DocForge CLI and Python distribution/import package.
Versioned HTTP, Tauri sidecar, and frontend workbench transport adapters.
Bundled docforge-standard template and repository-owned project fixtures.
api_contracts: The public command is docforge and no thesisforge command alias remains.
Project open accepts a directory or docforge.yaml and rejects bare Markdown and obsolete manifests.
CLI, HTTP, Tauri, and frontend fixtures share one versioned DocForge workbench protocol.
The public core aggregate is ForgeDocument and ThesisDocument is not exported.
Inspect, validate, review, and build continue to use the same deterministic application services.
database_entities: None; project state remains local files and in-memory domain objects.
permissions: Read only explicitly selected project-relative source, template, bibliography, and asset paths.
Write only explicit or manifest-resolved review and build outputs inside the permitted workspace boundary.
Reject absolute paths, remote paths, traversal, and symlink escapes without elevating operating-system permissions.
operational_constraints: Core inspect, validate, review, and build flows remain offline and require no AI service, API key, database, or network.
Failed builds preserve the previous successful output and never overwrite the source or manifest.
The parse, validate, resolve, compile, render, finalize, postflight, and preview stages remain ordered and deterministic.
The migration is a single breaking cutover with no dual loader, compatibility alias, or migration fallback.
Repository-owned examples, fixtures, tests, documentation, packaging, and CI move to the new contract in the same change.
data_flows: docforge.yaml -> project loader -> safe project-relative paths -> document Markdown and resources.
Markdown -> ForgeDocument -> validation -> template resolution -> RenderPlan -> DOCX.
Generic metadata -> template bindings without academic requirements.
Optional academic profile -> academic template bindings without parser or renderer special casing.
CLI or workbench intent -> shared application service -> DocForge protocol response and progress events.
Build result -> build/document.docx plus review/document.review.md and review/document.review-map.json defaults.
